resources.string: 1. Install Shizuku or a compatible service app. Some forks need a separate compatibility app; follow their instructions. Start it with wireless debugging or ADB, also on rooted phones: Android doesn’t allow clipboard reading from root. Run one service at a time.
2. Connect to Wi-Fi. In Android Settings, enable Developer options if needed, then enable Wireless debugging. The official guide explains where these settings are on your phone.
3. In Shizuku, choose Pairing. In Wireless debugging, choose Pair device with pairing code. Enter Android’s code in the service app. Other forks may use different steps.
4. Start your service and wait until it is running. If ClipHistory is not recognised after an update, restart the service. Pairing and starting are separate steps.

5. Return here and tap Connect. Allow ClipHistory to use the service, then run the Connection test. Recording stores text locally until it rolls out of your chosen limit or you delete it. Pause before copying private text that another app might not mark sensitive.
